concept: Depth policy that measures draft and verify cost per depth
summary: Ollama: cost is an EWMA of target-forward wall time per visited depth, read by piecewise-linear interpolation, flat outside the sampled range. Acceptance is a per-position conditional EWMA. Expected committed tokens at depth N are 1 plus the running product of position acceptances summed to N.

facts.text: Ollama: cost is an EWMA of target-forward wall time per visited depth, read by piecewise-linear interpolation, flat outside the sampled range. Acceptance is a per-position conditional EWMA. Expected committed tokens at depth N are 1 plus the running product of position acceptances summed to N.

Ollama: a depth is only costed when a round's depth equals the prior round's, so batch-shape transitions never enter the cost model; the controller seeds the shallowest unsampled depth to dwell there.
MTPLX: the policy had priced depth 2 below depth 3 although depth 2 ran the eager verifier and depth 3 the compiled fixed-M4 route; measuring per depth removed the mispricing.
MTPLX 2.11.2: measured costs, one-time compilation excluded, both depths re-probed; the 27B packs do not use this path.
Ollama: one stall-inflated cost sample could flip the comparison against plain decode and never heal once the controller stops parking at depth 0, hence the clamp.
Ollama: an unmeasured depth would always look best, so the search is capped at one past the acceptance frontier and at the drafter's limit.
Ollama: sessions with logprobs requests never draft and do not feed depth-0 cost.
Whether MTPLX's policy uses the same same-depth gate; the release notes do not say.
Ollama's cost EWMA weight is 0.3 (`costEWMAAlpha`) and one sample may move the estimate by at most 25 percent of its current value (`costClampFraction`).
The cost model is ready only after two distinct depths are sampled, and cost between samples is linearly interpolated.
Acceptance uses an EWMA weight of 0.1 per position, a position is trusted after 10 reaches (`acceptanceMinSamples`), and an under-sampled position inherits the deepest trusted rate, or 1 if none.
Only the surviving prefix is updated per round: position i is observed only if at least i-1 drafts were accepted.
The search limit is the acceptance frontier plus one, held to the drafter's limit, so depth climbs one position at a time.
Cost is recorded only when a round's draft depth matches the previous round's, and the controller drafts the shallowest unsampled depth to seed a clean sample.
The scheduled depth, cost curve, acceptance rates and probe cadence persist across requests in the speculation, and a new request starts at `depth.scheduled`.
A request with logprobs or top-logprobs keeps a speculation session only to maintain the draft cache and is permanently parked.
A round's draft is capped at remaining-1 tokens so the bonus token lands within the budget.
MTPLX 2.11.2 states the verify-cost mispricing and that `MTPLX_ADAPTIVE_VERIFY_COST_FEEDBACK=0` restores the configured prior.
MTPLX's trace report shows how many verify steps ran compiled and what a full round costs, and 2.12.0 adds an `mtp_pays` verdict comparing delivered tokens per second with a matched plain run.
